Sparse outside records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21M here to set up primary care. Moved into an apartment in Amherst this summer and his old pediatric/family doctor is two hours away; mostly he needs someone to keep writing his ADHD med.

ADHD, combined type: diagnosed around age 10, on Adderall IR 20 mg twice a day for years. Takes the second dose around 1 pm, says if he takes it later he doesn't sleep. Works construction (framing crew), says the med keeps him from making mistakes on the job. No palpitations, no chest pain, appetite fine, sleeping 6-7 hrs.

Allergies: seasonal hay fever in spring, uses cetirizine 10 mg when it's bad. Has an albuterol inhaler from his old doctor, uses it 'once in a while' when he has a cold, can't say why it was first given. No ED visits for breathing.

PMH: as above. PSH: T&A at age 8. Broke left forearm at 16 skateboarding, had plates put in (ORIF), no problems since.
Meds: Adderall 20 mg BID, cetirizine 10 mg prn, albuterol HFA prn.
Allergies: PCN (rash as a kid), sulfa (hives).
FH: dad - drinking problem, high BP. Mom - anxiety, thyroid (on replacement). Paternal grandfather had a heart attack at 54. No bleeding problems in the family, nobody with early osteoporosis that he knows of.
SH: single, lives with a roommate. Framing/construction laborer. Smokes about half a pack a day, started at 18. Drinks mostly on weekends, often 6-8 beers or more in a night; denies morning drinking, has never tried to cut down. No other drugs. On his mother's insurance through her job.

Exam: well-appearing, fidgety but pleasant. HEENT: TMs clear, mild boggy nasal mucosa. Neck supple. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd benign. Ext: healed scar volar L forearm. Skin no rash. Neuro grossly normal. Mood good, affect bright.

A/P
1. ADHD, combined - stable on current dose. Reviewed MA PMP, fills monthly from one pharmacy, consistent. Controlled substance agreement signed today. Will continue Adderall 20 mg BID, 30-day supply, visits q3-4 mo.
2. Tobacco use disorder - advised quitting, he's not interested right now. Will keep asking.
3. Alcohol use disorder, mild - AUDIT-C 6. Talked about binge pattern and the combination with stimulant. Not ready to change. Revisit.
4. Seasonal allergic rhinitis - cetirizine prn.
5. Albuterol prn - rarely used, will refill as needed.
6. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, GGT, HIV and hep C once today. Flu shot in October. Records requested from prior practice.

RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rowan - your bloodwork from Monday came back fine. Liver tests and GGT are normal, blood counts normal, kidney function normal, cholesterol fine for now. HIV and hepatitis C screens negative. Nothing to change. Talk soon.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside ED record, date of service 12/20/2021, received by fax.

22M, restrained driver, head-on collision. Knees struck dash. Severe R hip pain, unable to move R leg. Per EMS report, intoxicated. Hx ADHD, tobacco and alcohol use. Allergies PCN, sulfa.
VS stable. R leg shortened, internally rotated. Unable to dorsiflex R foot. Pelvis XR: posterior dislocation R hip.
Closed reduction under procedural sedation, successful. Post-reduction CT pelvis: concentric reduction, no acetabular or femoral head fracture. R foot dorsiflexion weakness persists post-reduction. Kept overnight for observation and pain control.
Dx: posterior dislocation R hip, reduced. R foot dorsiflexion weakness.
Dispo 12/21: home, crutches, toe-touch weight bearing R, ibuprofen 600 q8h prn. Ortho clinic 1 week. Return for worsening weakness or pain.

Pain 6/10 with ibuprofen. Ortho appt 12/29. Asked if he can still take Adderall with what they gave him - yes, nothing new besides ibuprofen. Booked with PCP 12/28. Asked ED to fax notes.

Now: hip pain 4/10, better. On crutches, toe-touch. Can't lift the front of his R foot. No back pain, no bladder or bowel change.
Exam: on crutches, uncomfortable getting onto table. R hip - not ranged today given recent reduction. R ankle dorsiflexion weak, plantarflexion 5/5. Pulses DP/PT 2+. L leg normal.
A/P: R posterior hip dislocation, s/p closed reduction, with R foot dorsiflexion weakness. Referral to ortho placed so it's in the system (appt tomorrow). PT per ortho. Ibuprofen as needed with food.
Alcohol: we talked about this one directly. He says it was a 'one-off.' Offered referral for counseling again - he'll think about it.
Out of work note through ortho visit. Continue Adderall.

conditions.label: Avascular necrosis of right femoral head

documents.title: Orthopedic Letter - MRI Hip (outside)
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,
Your patient Rowan Morrow had his surveillance MRI of the right hip on 4/19/2022. It shows avascular necrosis of the right femoral head, without subchondral collapse. There is no fracture. The left hip is normal.
We reviewed this with him. He has no hip pain at present. Plan is observation: avoid high-impact loading where he can (jumping down from height, running), and repeat radiographs in about a year, sooner if he develops groin pain.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa. Medications: amphetamine-dextroamphetamine 20 mg twice daily, cetirizine as needed, albuterol as needed.
Thank you for allowing us to see him.
Orthopedic Surgery

documents.title: hip mri
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ortho said my hip bone has avascular necrosis. what does that actually mean. will i need a new hip. hip doesn't even hurt

documents.title: RE: hip mri
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rowan - it means part of the ball of the hip joint lost some of its blood supply after the dislocation. Right now the shape of the bone is intact, which is the important part. Many people stay stable for a long time. The plan of watching it with x-rays and going easy on the hard pounding makes sense. Smoking and heavy drinking both make this kind of bone problem worse, so that's one more real reason to cut down - I'm glad to help any time you want. Let us know if you start getting groin or hip pain.

documents.title: ED Provider Note (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department, DOS 6/9/2023. Faxed to PCP.
24yo M, unrestrained driver, high-speed MVC, airbags deployed. Arrives alert but agitated, odor of alcohol. GCS 14 (E3 V5 M6). C/o neck pain. Forehead laceration. Denies LOC; cannot recall events before the crash. Hx limited/unreliable due to agitation and presumed intoxication.
Hx: ADHD, tobacco, alcohol use, AVN R femoral head. NKDA per pt initially - chart shows PCN, sulfa allergy.
VS: BP 130/85, HR 98, RR 16, SpO2 97% RA.
Exam: midline C-spine tenderness, no step-off, no crepitus. Neuro nonfocal. Forehead laceration.
CT head w/o contrast: no acute intracranial abnormality.
CT C-spine: nondisplaced fracture of the C6 vertebral body. No canal compromise. Alignment maintained.
Spine service consulted by phone: rigid cervical collar, outpatient spine follow-up 6-8 wks.
Laceration irrigated, repaired with simple interrupted sutures. Tdap given (last 2010).
Dx: C6 vertebral body fracture, nondisplaced. Forehead laceration, repaired.
Dispo: home with family member once sober, collar at all times, suture removal 7 days, spine clinic.

orders.reason: C6 vertebral body fracture, collar management

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED visit Friday night 6/9. Second crash in 18 months. He was driving, not belted, airbags went off. ED note received: C6 body fracture, nondisplaced, collar; forehead laceration sutured; Tdap given. He was drinking beforehand - he says 'a lot.'
Today: neck sore but better, in hard collar. No arm numbness or weakness. Remembers the evening but not the drive.
Exam: in collar, not removed. Forehead wound healing well, no erythema or drainage - sutures removed today, edges well apposed. Grip and arm strength 5/5 both sides, sensation intact. Gait steady.
A/P:
1. C6 vertebral body fracture - collar at all times. Referral placed to spine clinic per ED plan. Out of work; no driving in collar.
2. Forehead laceration - healed, sutures out.
3. Alcohol use disorder - AUDIT-C 7. Two crashes, both after drinking. Told him plainly I'm worried he will be killed or kill someone. Offered outpatient addiction treatment referral and discussed medication options; he declined both, though he listened. Will keep raising it.
4. ADHD - continue; he asked to keep it the same.
5. Tobacco - not ready.

documents.title: ED and Brief Hospital Summary (outside)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Outside hospital. Admit 6/22/2024, discharge 6/24/2024.
25M, high-speed MVC. Third crash-related visit in 2.5 years per records. Severe suprapubic pain, gross hematuria.
PMH: ADHD, tobacco use, alcohol use disorder, R femoral head AVN, prior C6 fracture. Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.
ED: hemodynamically stable, in distress from pain. Abdomen soft, suprapubic tenderness, no rebound or guarding. Pelvic XR: R pubic rami fracture. FAST negative for free fluid. Foley placed - gross hematuria.
CT cystogram: extraperitoneal bladder rupture. No intraperitoneal extravasation.
Urology: nonoperative, catheter drainage ~2 weeks, cystogram before removal.
Ortho: pelvic fracture nonoperative, WBAT.
Course uneventful. Discharged home with indwelling Foley and leg bag. Urology f/u for cystogram in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Admission 6/22/2025 - 7/2/2025, neurocritical care. Received by fax 8/12/2025.
26M, unrestrained driver, car versus tree. Found unresponsive; intubated for airway protection.
PMH: ADHD, tobacco and alcohol use disorders, R femoral head AVN, prior C6 fracture, prior extraperitoneal bladder rupture. Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.
Exam on arrival: pupils equal and reactive; no purposeful response to painful stimulus.
CT head without contrast: no skull fracture, no large focal hematoma; multiple small punctate hemorrhages at the gray-white matter junction and in deep brain structures.
Hospital course: remained comatose for more than 48 hours despite normalized vital signs; repeat CT without new findings. Findings consistent with diffuse axonal injury. Began following commands on hospital day 6, extubated day 7. Stimulant held during the stay.
Discharge diagnosis: diffuse axonal injury.
Disposition: to acute inpatient rehabilitation.

documents.title: Call from mother
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's mother called (pt listed her as contact). Rowan was in another car accident Saturday night, in ICU, on a breathing machine, has a brain injury. She wanted us to know. Offered support; asked that the hospital send records when he's discharged. Message to PCP.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aware. Will follow up with family after discharge. Hold stimulant refills until we see him.

documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Acute rehab 7/2/2025 - 7/23/2025, after diffuse axonal injury from MVC 6/22.
Program: daily PT, OT and speech therapy.
At discharge: ambulating independently, independent in self-care, oriented, following multistep commands. Neurologic exam without focal deficit.
Medications at discharge: amphetamine-dextroamphetamine 20 mg twice daily resumed, cetirizine as needed, albuterol as needed.
Discharged home with mother. Outpatient therapy and neurology follow-up arranged.

procedures.procedure: Transitional care management, high complexity

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26M with his mother. Car vs tree 6/22, ICU then rehab, home 7/23. Hospital summaries not yet received; history from pt, mother and the discharge papers they brought: diffuse axonal injury, coma for a couple of days, off the ventilator after about a week, three weeks rehab.
He doesn't remember the crash or most of the ICU. Walking on his own. Staying at his mother's.
Meds per discharge papers: Adderall 20 BID (rehab restarted it), cetirizine prn, albuterol prn. Reconciled.
Exam: alert, oriented x3, conversant. Pupils equal, reactive. EOM full. Face symmetric. Strength 5/5 all four limbs. Sensation intact. Finger-nose normal. Gait normal, tandem ok.
A/P:
1. Diffuse axonal injury - neuro exam nonfocal today. Outpatient therapy and neurology follow-up already set by rehab.
2. ADHD - continue Adderall 20 BID as restarted.
3. Alcohol use disorder - four crashes now. Discussed with him and his mother present, with his OK. He says he hasn't had a drink since the accident. Addiction medicine referral offered; he wants to wait.
4. Tobacco - not ready.
No work for now; follow neurology guidance. RTC after neurology visit or sooner.

Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

procedures.procedure: Initial hospital inpatient care

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: pulmonary and critical care
documents.body:
Admitted 6/23/2026, discharged 7/2/2026. Services: orthopedic surgery, pulmonary/critical care.

27M brought in after a high-speed MVC with a closed displaced fracture of the R femoral shaft. Background of yearly crashes since 2021: R hip dislocation with later R femoral head AVN, C6 fracture, extraperitoneal bladder rupture, diffuse axonal injury (2025). Also ADHD, tobacco and alcohol use disorders, seasonal allergic rhinitis. Allergies: penicillin (rash), sulfa (hives). Home meds: amphetamine-dextroamphetamine 20 mg BID, cetirizine 10 mg daily prn, albuterol HFA prn.

Course: splinted, IV fluids and analgesia while awaiting fixation. Around 36 hours after injury (morning of 6/25) he became acutely short of breath and confused. SpO2 88% on room air, RR 30, HR 110, BP 130/85. Bilateral crackles. Disoriented to time and place at intervals, no focal neurologic deficit. Petechiae across the neck, anterior chest and axillae.
ABG on room air: pH 7.45, PaCO2 32, PaO2 60, HCO3 24.
CXR: bilateral diffuse infiltrates.
Diagnosis: fat embolism syndrome. Transferred to ICU, high-flow nasal oxygen; not intubated. Oxygenation and mental status improved over the next three days.
Intramedullary nailing of the R femur 6/28, uncomplicated. Weaned to room air.

Discharge: home, crutches, WBAT R leg. Oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 1-2 tabs q6h prn, short supply. Resume home meds. Ortho clinic 6 weeks with x-rays. PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Orthopedic Post-op Note (outside)
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body: Ortho clinic 8/11/2026, 6 weeks s/p IM nailing R femoral shaft fracture. Off opioids. Ambulating with one crutch. Incisions healed. Knee and hip ROM functional. XR R femur: early callus, alignment maintained, nail and screws intact. Advance weight bearing, wean crutch, PT. Return 6 weeks with x-rays. Off work until next visit.
